title: ImageNet-trained CNNs are biased towards texture; increasing shape bias improves accuracy and robustness (Geirhos et al., ICLR 2019)
relevant_finding: In cue-conflict images, ImageNet CNNs classify mostly by texture where humans use shape; training on Stylized-ImageNet raises shape bias.
experimental_setting: ImageNet CNN classifiers on style-transferred cue-conflict images; not VLMs, not driving scenes.
use_here: Motivation for appearance-vs-geometry manipulation. NOT evidence that our model is texture-biased; our prompt intervention is not a shape-bias training method.

title: Robust Physical-World Attacks on Deep Learning Visual Classification (Eykholt et al., CVPR 2018)
relevant_finding: Optimised physical stickers on stop signs caused targeted misclassification of specific classifiers under varied viewpoints.
experimental_setting: Adversarially optimised perturbations against specific road-sign classifiers.
use_here: Distinguishes adversarial attacks from our non-optimised, procedural appearance variants. We perform no adversarial optimisation and modify no real signs.

title: Phantom of the ADAS: Securing Advanced Driver-Assistance Systems from Split-Second Phantom Attacks (Nassi et al., ACM CCS 2020)
relevant_finding: Commercial ADAS (Tesla HW2.5/3, Mobileye 630) treated depthless projected/billboard-embedded objects as real; proposed a light/context/surface/depth committee detector.
experimental_setting: Projectors and digital billboards against commercial ADAS; real vehicles.
use_here: Closest prior motivation for the flat_depiction family (depictions treated as physical). Our results are synthetic and do not reproduce or test any commercial ADAS.

title: Benchmarking Neural Network Robustness to Common Corruptions and Perturbations (Hendrycks & Dietterich, ICLR 2019)
relevant_finding: ImageNet-C/-P benchmark ordinary corruptions (noise, blur, weather) separately from worst-case adversarial perturbations.
use_here: Taxonomy: our dusk/back-lit lighting is an ordinary condition change, not a corruption benchmark or adversarial attack.

title: Training Deep Networks with Synthetic Data: Bridging the Reality Gap by Domain Randomization (Tremblay et al., CVPR-W 2018)
relevant_finding: Synthetic imagery differs from real imagery (reality gap); non-realistic randomisation used to make detectors rely on essential features.
experimental_setting: Car detection trained on synthetic data, evaluated on KITTI.
use_here: Supports our main limitation: low-poly flat-shaded rendering is itself a domain shift; the model may judge rendering style, not physical structure.

title: Ollama library: nemotron3 (tag 33b)
relevant_finding: nemotron3:33b listed as 28GB, 128K context, inputs Text, Image; described as NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Nano Omni (video/audio/image/text).
use_here: Runtime/model provenance. Local `ollama show` reported architecture nemotron_h_omni, 33.0B, Q4_K_M, capability vision, NVIDIA Open Model License.

title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Nano Omni documentation (NeMo Megatron-Bridge)
relevant_finding: 30B-A3B MoE multimodal reasoning model; Mamba/attention hybrid backbone with RADIO vision tower; image/video/audio/text inputs.
use_here: Model capability context; image support was additionally verified locally with an actual image request.
